To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SSB protein from Aquifex aeoli- cus has been overexpresscd, purified and crystallized in both the absence (native) and presence (DNA-bound) of DNA.
the full-length A. aeolicus SSB has been overexpresssed, purified and crystallized.
a full-length SSB protein from a thermophilic bacterium has been cloned, over-expressed and purified and crystals have been obtained.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the structural and functional basis of the thermostability of the SSB protein from A. aeolicus.
the molecular basis for the extreme thermostability of the A. aeolicus SSB and the mechanism by which it binds to ssDNA.
understanding how SSB proteins from hyperthermophiles function in their native environments, which are at much higher temperatures than those of their mesophilic homologues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SSB protein from A. aeolicus has the potential to be a good model for the structural study of DNA binding and that the DNA-bound form is a particularly good candidate for structure determination.
SSB from A. aeolicus is a tetramer in solution as well as in the crystal, and that the DNA is bound to one face of the protein.
the crystal structure of the SSB from A. aeolicus has provided an insight into the mechanism of DNA binding and DNA stabilization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SSB protein from A. aeolicus is the smallest and simplest SSB protein known to date.
we have solved the structure of a hyperthermophile protein and we have also solved the structure of an SSB in complex with its ligand, ssDNA, and that this is a first for any SSB.
we have cloned, expressed and purified the full-length SSB protein from Aquifex aeoli...
The main takeaway from our work is that
SSB proteins from hyperthermophiles can be overexpressed and crystallized and that the crystals are of good quality.
the SSB protein from A. aeolicus has a high thermal stability (Tm = 90 degrees C) and can form crystals in the presence of ssDNA.
it is possible to grow high-quality crystals of hyperthermophillic proteins at ambient temperatures.
